walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Distributions — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Distributions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Distributions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of (3x + 1)^2 with respect to x?
options: 4.65, because rounding to 1 dp means cutting after the second decimal.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
The derivative is 2(3x + 1) — applying the power rule without the chain rule.
6(3x + 1) — by the chain rule, multiplying by the derivative of the inside (3).

mcqs.q: If 5 pens cost £3.50, how much do 7 pens cost?
options: £24.50, by multiplying £3.50 by 7.
£4.90 — find the unit cost (£0.70 per pen), then multiply by 7.
4.65, because rounding to 1 dp means cutting after the second decimal.
£5.50, by adding £2 to £3.50 because there are 2 more pens.
4.6 — look at the second decimal (4), which is less than 5, so round down.
£24.50, by multiplying £3.50 by 7.
4.65, because rounding to 1 dp means cutting after the second decimal.
4.7, because the 8 at the end rounds the 4 up to 5, which then rounds the 6 up to 7.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Variance”?
options: E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability mass function”?
options: PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
